subject.title: fix(gateway): bound connect frame auth.* fields at the protocol schema

question: Should connect-frame auth bounds be enforced as byte/ASCII token-shape limits across all six auth fields, or are grapheme maxLength caps acceptable for this pre-auth security boundary?
rationale: The PR changes security-sensitive gateway handshake validation and existing client compatibility, and the current implementation does not align the schema limit unit with the byte-based comparison work it is meant to bound.

options.title: Require byte or token-shape bounds
options.body: Update the schema/test shape so the pre-auth boundary rejects oversized byte payloads or non-token-shaped values before secret comparison work, then review the chosen limits.

options.title: Accept grapheme maxLength caps
options.body: Maintain the current TypeBox maxLength approach and explicitly own the residual byte-amplification and compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Narrow the capped field set
options.body: Limit this PR to the originally proven auth fields and track runtime-token limits separately with their owner-specific contract.

recommendation.title: Require byte or token-shape bounds
recommendation.body: Update the schema/test shape so the pre-auth boundary rejects oversized byte payloads or non-token-shaped values before secret comparison work, then review the chosen limits.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway protocol package and schema history makes this the strongest available owner for the protocol-boundary decision, with joshavant relevant for the runtime identity field.
